sc: 7-year-old girl, brief stares many times a day, no post-ictal phase, 3 Hz spike-wave → Absence epilepsy: ethosuximide/valproate
Infant with clusters of jerks on waking, ash-leaf spots → West syndrome (tuberous sclerosis)
Toddler turns blue and limp after crying → Breath-holding spell (not epilepsy)
f: ≥ 2 unprovoked seizures > 24 h apart (or one with high recurrence risk)
West (3–12 mo, spasms, hypsarrhythmia) · absence (3 Hz) · juvenile myoclonic (morning jerks, teen) · Rolandic (night face twitching)
EEG · MRI if focal or abnormal exam · glucose, calcium · ECG for faints
Generalised: valproate 20–40 mg/kg/day · focal: carbamazepine 10–20 mg/kg/day · phenobarbitone 3–5 · West: ACTH/vigabatrin
Phenytoin: gum hypertrophy, hirsutism · carbamazepine: hyponatraemia, rash · valproate: liver failure (< 2 yr), weight gain · phenobarbitone: hyperactivity
trap: Carbamazepine worsens absence and myoclonic seizures · breath-holding spells and syncope are not epilepsy · valproate in girls: teratogenic
